spec.name: Convoy Hauler MK-IV 'Warden'
spec.description: A low-poly cyberpunk armoured six-wheel convoy hauler with a wedge cab, roof gun turret and a sealed, glowing cargo pod strapped on its flatbed.
spec.layout: Long heavy truck facing +Z. Front: angular wedge cab with a sloped armoured windscreen (cyan glowing visor strip), a bull-bar ram with yellow hazard stripes and twin headlights. Cab roof carries a ring-mounted twin-barrel turret. Behind the cab a low flatbed chassis with three axles (one front steering, two rear) on chunky faceted wheels with glowing neon hub rings. The back half is a big rounded-box sealed cargo pod held by four yellow cargo straps and corner clamps, with a magenta glowing seal-lock band and a hazard-marked door at the rear. Hull is dark gunmetal panelled steel with yellow hazard trim, cyan and magenta neon strips along skirts, antennas and tail lights. Everything is chunky faceted primitives, panel paints, SVG decals (hazard stripes, serial numbers, kanji-like glyph labels) and glow on lights and screens.

parts.builds: The frame and flatbed: ladder frame rails, deck plate (panelled gunmetal paint with rivets), side skirts with cyan neon strip and yellow hazard-stripe SVG trim, fender arches over each of the six wheels, fuel and battery boxes between axles, exposed underbody cables and drive shafts, rear bumper with magenta-red tail lights (glowing) and a tow hitch, mud flaps, ladder step and grab rails. Includes the axle beams and suspension springs (coil sweeps) for all three axles, but not the wheels.
parts.attaches: Cab sits on it at cabBack/chassisTop forward end; pod rests on podBase; wheels mount on axleFront, axleMid, axleRear lines. Rides joint body.

parts.builds: The wedge armoured cab: lofted sloped hull with chamfered faceted panels, steeply raked armoured windscreen with glowing cyan visor strip and SVG HUD-like glyph texture, slit side windows with cage bars, side doors with yellow hazard decals and serial-number text, mirrors with small glowing screens, roof light bar (magenta/cyan glow), roof antennas and sensor dome, vents, a ram bull-bar bumper with hazard stripes, twin headlights (glow) and a grille with painted mesh. Roof has the turretRing seat plate.
parts.attaches: Sits on chassis at cabBack; roof ring plate at turretRing/cabRoof where turret mounts; bumper at bumper mount. Rides joint cab.

parts.builds: Roof-mounted remote gun turret: round lathe base ring with yellow chevron paint, rotating faceted armoured housing on turretYaw, twin barrels with muzzle brakes, heat-shield sleeves and ammo box on side with feed belt, pitch cradle on gunPitch with a small sensor camera with glowing cyan lens, warning red lamp, antenna whip. Barrels point +Z in rest pose.
parts.attaches: Base ring seated on turretRing mount over the cab roof. Rides turretYaw (housing) and gunPitch (barrels, cradle).

parts.builds: Six chunky low-poly wheels: faceted 10-sided tyres with rubber tread paint, steel rims with bolt rings, hub caps, glowing neon cyan (front) and magenta (rear) hub-ring accents, brake discs with yellow calipers visible behind spokes, reinforced mudguard-height sidewall armour plates. Each wheel built on its own wheel joint, axle line along x, wheel radius 0.55 so bottoms touch y=0. Rear four are dual-tyred (two tyres per side per axle).
parts.attaches: Hubs at axleFront, axleMid, axleRear with x = ±1.3; tyres' outer face about x ±1.65. Rides wheelFL, wheelFR, wheelML, wheelMR, wheelRL, wheelRR.

parts.builds: The sealed cargo pod: long rounded-box shell of light podShell paint with panelled seams, rounded end caps, four yellow cargo straps with ratchet buckles and corner clamp brackets, saddles/cradles on the deck, a magenta glowing seal-lock band around the middle with SVG biohazard/lock glyphs, label decals (serial numbers, BIOHAZARD/PRIORITY stripes in SVG), reinforced rear double door on podDoor hinge with glowing lock bars and red warning light, roof vents, small status screens glowing green-cyan, tie-down rings and a small sensor mast. Looks tightly sealed and valuable.
parts.attaches: Rests on the chassis deck at podBase; front face near podFront behind the cab; rear door hinge at podDoor. Rides body, with the door on podDoor.

Given the loft approach seemed uncertain, I decide instead to write a rounded-box helper that extrudes a rounded rectangle shape to form the shell, then position it in the scene using those size and location parameters, applying a panelled paint texture from the kit for rivets and detail.

For the front face I'm considering rounded edge caps and a darker reinforcing bumper panel frame to give the front end more structure.

Now I'm figuring out side placement for straps, bands, and decal glyphs, positioning them along the z-axis so the serial text, straps, and biohazard glyph circles don't overlap on the panel face.

Adding a glowing green screen panel and a BIOHAZARD label plate, then working out the text orientation logic for each side of the plane based on viewing direction and up-axis mapping before finalizing the compact label text for both sides.

I'm planning the chassis dimensions, setting up the body box bounds and wheel positions with their radii to keep everything proportioned correctly.

Now I'm laying out the frame rails, deck plate, side skirts between the wheel arches, and thinking through how to add fender arches using half-cylinder geometry over each wheel.

Checking fender clearance against the deck edges and dual rear tyre spacing to make sure nothing overlaps outside the box limits, then moving on to placing the axle beams connecting the wheels.

Now I'm defining spring coils between the axles and body using a clockwork kit import, panelling the deck with the hull color, and setting up a diagonal yellow-and-dark hazard stripe texture for the skirt.

I'm defining rod and cable helpers, where rods take two endpoints with a radius and color, and cables sweep through a Catmull-Rom curve with a thin radius. I'm also making sure the rear dual-tyred axles have fenders spanning both sides correctly before writing the final code.

spec.name: Hoverback Raider
spec.description: A militarized pickup truck converted to ride on four ducted hover thrusters, low-poly cyberpunk with neon underglow, armor plates and a roof-mounted gun.
spec.layout: A boxy armored pickup seen from the side: long hood at the front (+Z), a two-door cab in the middle, an open cargo bed at the back with a roll bar and a pintle gun. The truck body floats about 0.55 m above the ground. Instead of wheels, four large ducted thrusters sit at the corners (wheel positions), each a ring shroud with a glowing cyan core and fan blades, angled slightly so they read as hover pods. The lowest points are the thruster pods, which rest at y=0 (floor); the chassis underside floats above. Style: faceted low-poly boxes and wedges, matte dark gunmetal hull with hazard-yellow trim, magenta and cyan neon strips, emissive glow on the thruster cores, headlights, taillights and underglow. Textured SVG decals: kanji/stencil numbers, hazard stripes, a magenta emblem on the doors, a HUD-lit windshield. Paints: scuffed metal, rust near the lower edges, panel seams and rivets.

Everything below y=1.0 between the thrusters except the thrusters themselves.

Pods are about 0.9 m wide and 0.5 m tall; their lowest points touch y=0. Mirrored with s=[1,-1] and front/back. Includes the thin mount arm from each pod to the chassis strut end.
parts.attaches: Each pod centred on its thrusterXX mount and joint; arms meet the chassis struts at x=±0.85.

parts.builds: The crew cab and hood: sloped armored hood with raised centre scoop, vents and a hazard-yellow stripe, front grille with glowing lamp slits, two rectangular headlights (glow lampWhite), angular windshield with slits and HUD texture glow, side windows with armored shutters, door panels with door lines, handles, a magenta emblem decal and stencil number, wing mirrors with small cyan screens, roof plate with rack, light bar (neon), antennas, fender flares over the thruster mounts, side exhaust stacks. Panelled gunmetal paint with scuffs and rust at the bottom edge.
parts.attaches: Sits on chassisTop. Rear wall at cabRear/bedFront meets the bed's front wall. Roof at roofTop.

parts.builds: The cargo bed and rear: open bed floor with ribbed texture, side walls with armor plates and slotted tie-downs, tailgate with hazard stripes and a lowered ramp detail, roll bar hoops behind the cab with trim and spotlights, cargo crates and fuel canisters strapped inside (olive, trim), taillights (glow lampRed) with neon strip across the tailgate, rear bumper, licence plate decal with kanji text, antenna whip with a small flag, and a rear thruster-vent cowl.
parts.attaches: Front wall touches the cab at bedFront. Floor at bedFloor over chassisTop. Roll bar frame stands at gunMount's front.

parts.builds: A pintle-mounted heavy gun on the bed: swivel base ring with ammo drum, pedestal, armored gun shield with trim stripes and a cyan sight slit, twin barrels with muzzle brakes and cooling sleeves, ammo belt of brass links curving into the receiver, a small radar dish and targeting module with a glowing magenta eye, handles, and a neon status light. All on the 'gun' joint so it can aim; the base is rigid on body.
parts.attaches: Base on bedFloor at gunMount; the roll bar sits just forward of it.

I'm also picking a small color palette with brass tones and glow accents for the eye, slit, and status light, plus planning a hazard-stripe texture for the shield's front face.

Next I'm figuring out the ammo belt and drum placement -- routing brass belt links along a curved path from the ammo drum to the receiver, and deciding how to use the along-path helper with frame positioning. Then I'm sketching out the lathe profile for the base ring, defining its outline points and bone attachment to keep the construction straightforward.

Now I'm laying out the gun's mechanical frame: a pedestal cylinder, a rotating turntable ring on the gun joint, and the receiver box positioned behind it. I'm adding yoke cheek plates flanking the turntable and extruding a shield shape from a polygon outline, along with planning a sight slit cut into it.

Still refining the shield slit and barrel geometry, using plain colored paint with scuff noise texture for the shield and a hazard stripe plane on its lower front, then sketching barrel sweeps and brake/sleeve details at the muzzle ends.

Now I'm adding the brake with vent fins, rear handle grips and spade grips built from looped rods, and sketching a radar dish on a stalk mounted atop the shield.

I need to recheck the vertical stacking so the dish stays within the 2.1 height limit—adjusting the shield top, stalk length, and dish radius so everything fits. Then I'm figuring out where to place a small targeting module box on top of the receiver, near the shield area toward the back.

Since the shield blocks a front-facing eye, I'll move the module onto the top of the shield instead, offset to one side, with a glowing magenta eye sphere peeking out front and a cyan status light placed opposite the radar piece.

Behind it a long low chassis (z -4.2..2.6) carries six chunky wheels in three pairs (front z=2.6, middle z=-0.4, rear z=-3.4), wheel radius 0.55, resting on y=0. Above the chassis a turntable ring at z=-1.0 carries a rotating turret base and a long railgun cradle; twin parallel rails run forward over the cab to z=4.6 and rearward with a capacitor bank behind. Four stabiliser legs fold out diagonally from the chassis sides at mid and rear, ending in broad foot pads on the floor (y=0). Style: faceted chunky panels, olive-drab hull with dark-grey armour plates, hazard yellow stripes on stabilisers and edges, cyan glowing energy strips on rails and capacitors, stencil markings and rivets painted via textures. I'm working out how to build the stabilizer geometry attached to the existing stabFL joint using its position and direction, constructing rods and parts in model space relative to the bone, keeping the structure compact.

I'm designing each stabilizer leg per side with a hinge point near the chassis, an upper arm extending to an elbow, a piston sleeve angling down to a foot pad with a ball joint, and a diagonal brace connecting the lower chassis to the piston mid-point, while keeping all elements within sensible height bounds relative to the hinge.

Now I'm detailing the piston as a thicker sleeve from elbow to midpoint and a thinner steel rod from midpoint to foot, adding hazard-stripe paint texture along a diagonal axis, and planning a chevron texture plane on top of the foot pad plus small ribs along its underside.

I'm defining the pad geometry more precisely—cylinder dimensions, chevron plane placement, ribs, bolt ring—and settling on an orange glowing beacon sphere, then sketching helper functions for drawing rods and frustum boxes between points with octagonal cross-sections.

spec.name: Warhound MX-77 Armored Truck
spec.description: A low-poly cyberpunk militarized 6x6 truck from 2077: angular armored hull, slab-sided cab with neon visor, roof turret, and a cargo bed with missile pods, antennas, and glowing trim.
spec.layout: A long, low-slung 6x6 armored truck facing +Z. Front (z 3.2 to 4.0): sloped armored bumper with a plow wedge, a winch, and a cyan light bar. Cab (z 0.9 to 3.2): a wedge-shaped, angular armored cab with a slanted windscreen drawn as a glowing cyan SVG visor slit, side armor plates with chevron decals, and a roof sensor mast. Behind the cab on the roof (z about -0.3 to 0.9) sits a rotating turret ring carrying a twin-barrel cannon and a sensor head. Cargo bed (z -4.0 to 0.9): an armored box with ribbed side panels, a rear missile pod rack, a folded antenna array and a hazard-striped tailgate with magenta tail lights. Running gear: three axles (front z 2.4, mid z -0.9, rear z -2.7) with six big chunky low-poly tyres on hexagonal rims, wheel arches with armor skirts, and a visible chassis frame with a drive shaft and fuel tank. Style: chunky faceted slabs in dark gunmetal with warning-yellow trim, cyan and magenta neon strips, panel seams and rivets via the panelled paint, SVG decals (hazard stripes, unit numbers, kanji-like glyphs, barcode labels), and glow on lights, visor, and the engine vents. Everything is crisp low-poly with beveled plates.

parts.builds: The running gear: a ladder-frame chassis with two long side rails, cross members, a drive shaft, differentials at each axle, fuel tank and battery boxes, leaf-spring suspension blocks, plus six large low-poly tyres (octagonal-tread lathe/cylinders with tread blocks, hex rims with bolts, glowing cyan hub caps) each on its wheel joint. Includes wheel arch liners, mud flaps with SVG hazard decals, and underbody glowing orange engine vents. Tyres use rubber with a paint for grime near the ground; frame uses metal('iron') and panelled paint.
parts.attaches: Top face meets cab, bed and hull skirts at chassisTop. Wheels ride wheelFL..wheelRR on axleFront, axleMid, axleRear. Front end meets the bumper at bumperBase; rear meets the tailgate mount.

parts.builds: The armored cab: a wedge-shaped faceted body (loft/extrudes) with a sloped hood, steeply raked windscreen holding a glowing cyan SVG visor slit with scanlines and HUD glyphs, side windows as narrow slits, thick side armor plates with yellow chevron decals and unit numbers, door seams, handles, roof rails, a roof sensor mast with a lidar disc, side mirrors as camera pods, an exhaust stack pair behind the cab, and a roof searchlight. Hull paint panelled over metal('iron') with hull colours, and trim stripes in yellow. Includes headlights as glowing cyan panels.
parts.attaches: Sits on cabFloor/chassisTop; its rear wall meets the bed at bedFront; roof at cabRoof; front meets the bumper at bumperBase.

parts.builds: The front assembly: a heavy sloped armored bumper and a wedge plow with layered plates, hazard-striped SVG decal, a winch drum with cable and hook, a cyan LED light bar, tow hooks, two fog light pods, a grille with glowing orange slats, skid plates, front fender armor over the first axle arches, and side step plates running back along the cab, with rivets and bolts as merged small parts.
parts.attaches: Back face meets the cab and chassis at bumperBase (z 3.2); sits above the front wheels' axle line at axleFront.

parts.builds: The armored cargo bed: a box body with ribbed side panels (repeated extruded ribs), slanted upper edges, top hatch doors with yellow trim, side equipment lockers with barcode and warning SVG labels, fuel and ammo crates, a rear missile pod rack with two angled 6-tube pods (glowing orange tube ends), a folded antenna array and radome dish, rear glowing magenta tail light bars, a hazard-striped tailgate on the tailgate joint with latches, rear bumper, and wheel-arch fender skirts over the middle and rear axles. Panelled hull paint with soot near the exhaust and orange glow strips along the lower flank.
parts.attaches: Floor rests on bedFloor/chassisTop; front wall meets the cab at bedFront; the roof's turret opening is at turretRing; the tailgate hinges at tailgate; pods at rearPods.

parts.builds: The roof weapon station on turretRing: a faceted turret ring base with gear teeth (the clockwork gearGeometry or ring of teeth), a rotating armored housing (angular extrude plates, yellow trim, kill-mark SVG decals), twin cannon barrels with muzzle brakes, heat-shield sleeves, glowing orange muzzle tips, a coaxial sensor head with a glowing magenta lens eye decal, ammo belt feed box with brass rounds, side smoke dischargers, a small antenna and a comms dish. Housing rides turretYaw, barrels and sensors ride gunPitch.
parts.attaches: Base ring sits on the roof at turretRing, between cab roof and cargo bed front; joints turretYaw and gunPitch.

calls.reasoning:
I'm defining a single buildTurret function that sets up the turret yaw and gun pitch joints with their positions and directions, relying on the Ctx type provided by the module rather than importing it.

Now I'm sketching the geometry: a boxy housing spanning roughly ±0.9 in x and from y 2.4 to 3.1, with a gear ring (36 teeth, radius 0.62) mounted on the turret yaw bone and a static base ring on the body, plus an extruded housing profile built from the turret pivot outward along the z-axis.

Working out dimensions for the gun housing, barrels, and mantlet -- placing the barrels at x ±0.2 extending from z 0.7 to 1.9 along the pitch bone, with thicker sleeve rods and a muzzle brake capping the front.

Now I'm adding the sensor head, positioning it off to one side near the top of the housing at roughly x=0.55, y=2.95, z=0.9, using the same rod/cylinder helper that orients parts along a bone direction.

Next I'm placing the ammo box on the left side with olive coloring and brass-colored merged cylinders for rounds, plus a feed chute connecting to the barrel, and defining a new brass color for this purpose. Then I'm sketching out smoke discharger tubes mounted in angled sets on either side of the rear housing.

Now I'm adding a tilted antenna rod near the top rear, and a small comms dish mounted on a post using a lathe-generated profile shaped like a shallow dish, making sure the outline points don't self-intersect.

For decals, I'm placing kill-mark planes on the housing sides at x=±0.505 facing outward, tied to the turret yaw bone so they rotate correctly, plus thin yellow trim boxes along the top edges. For the sensor lens, I'm considering a magenta radial glow using the glow kit so the eye reads as an emissive light source.

For the roof, I'm lathing a hatch circle on top of the housing. For paint, I'm testing a panelled iron metal versus a mottled hull-color blend to decide which reads better on the housing surface, then extruding the housing profile along the model's Z axis with the rear bustle as a separate lower extrusion piece and adding angled front plate layers.

Adding side armor plates...

Now I'm working out the vertical placement of the gear housing relative to the gun barrel pivot -- the housing needs to sit below the gun axis so the mantlet aligns correctly, so I'm adjusting the profile heights and letting the mantlet box be centered on the gun axis with the housing front sloping down toward the back.

Still writing barrel geometry...

Still positioning components...

Still placing antenna and dish pieces...
